page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable x86_64 cloud server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance features 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, supported by 128 GB of DDR5 memory configured at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4 GB per vCPU). Hardware capabilities include 105 MB of L3 cache alongside Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. It operates without dedicated local NVMe storage and includes a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7i-flex.8xlarge demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, placing in the top quartile for single-core Geekbench tasks (2023.0 score), single-threaded gzip compression (32.42 GB/sec), image processing, and static web serving throughput (48.18 GB/sec). Multi-threaded workloads and raw memory bandwidth sit within average benchmark tiers, with large-block uncached read and write bandwidth reaching 170.39 GB/sec and 89.67 GB/sec respectively. Small LLM text generation performs efficiently, whereas text generation on larger 70B models shows resource constraints at 2.67 tokens per second. The burstable CPU allocation provides cost efficiency for variable workloads, though sustained peak compute utilization may encounter performance throttling.
The resource balance makes this instance suitable for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, light-to-medium database instances, application servers, and lightweight AI inference tasks.
